paragraphs.sourceText: Our brains respond to language expressing facts differently than they do to words conveying possibility, scientists at New York University have recently found. Their work offers new insights into the impact word choice has on how we 26 between statements expressing what is real versus what is merely possible. The researchers assert their findings are important because we are presented with false information all the time. Some of this is 27 , as is the case with deceptive advertisements, but the problem is 28 by individuals who believe they are sharing correct information. Thus, it is more important than ever to separate the factual from the possible or merely 29 in how we communicate. This is especially true as the study makes clear that information presented as fact 30 special responses in our brains, which are distinct from when we process the same content with clear indicators of 31 .
paragraphs.translationZh: 纽约大学的科学家最近发现，我们的大脑对表达事实的语言的反应与对表达可能性的词语的反应不同。他们的工作为我们如何区分表达真实与仅仅可能的陈述的影响提供了新的见解。研究人员声称他们的发现很重要，因为我们一直收到虚假信息。其中一些是故意的，就像欺骗性广告的情况一样，但如果个人认为自己正在分享正确的信息，问题就会更加严重。因此，在我们的沟通方式中，将事实与可能的或仅仅是推测的分开比以往任何时候都更加重要。尤其如此，因为研究清楚地表明，作为事实呈现的信息会在我们的大脑中引起特殊的反应，这与我们处理具有明确的不确定性指标的相同内容时不同。

paragraphs.sourceText: In their new study, the scientists intended to 32 how the brain computes possibilities as expressed by words such as “may,” “might,” and “if.” The researchers compared brain responses to statements expressing factual 33 and those expressing possibility. “There is a monster under my bed” exemplifies a factual statement. “I will stay home,” is also factual. This is opposed to statements that express possibility, like “There might be a monster under my bed,” or “If it rains, I will stay home.” The results of the study showed that factual language 34 a rapid increase in brain activity, with the brain responding more powerfully and showing more engagement with factual phrases compared to those communicating possibility. Thus, facts rule when it comes to the brain. Brain regions involved in processing 35 rapidly distinguish facts from possibilities. Further, these regions respond in a much more robust fashion to factual statements.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在他们的新研究中，科学家们打算确定大脑如何计算“可能”、“可能”和“如果”等词语所表达的可能性。研究人员比较了大脑对表达事实场景和表达可能性的陈述的反应。 “我的床底下有一个怪物”是事实陈述的例证。 “我会呆在家里”也是事实。这与表达可能性的陈述相反，例如“我的床底下可能有怪物”或“如果下雨，我会呆在家里”。研究结果表明，事实语言激活了大脑活动的快速增加，与那些交流可能性相比，大脑的反应更强烈，并且对事实短语的参与程度更高。因此，当涉及到大脑时，事实占主导地位。参与处理话语的大脑区域可以快速区分事实和可能性。此外，这些地区对事实陈述的反应更加强烈。

paragraphs.sourceText: African countries must get smarter with their agriculture
paragraphs.translationZh: 非洲国家的农业必须变得更加聪明

paragraphs.sourceText: A) On the hills of central Kenya, almost lime-green with the sparkle of tea bushes in the sunlight, farmers know all about climate change. “The rainy season is no longer predictable,” says one. “When it is supposed to rain it doesn’t, then it all comes at once.” Climate change is an issue that will affect everyone on the planet. For Africans its consequences will be particularly bitter: whereas other regions were able to grow rich by burning coal and oil, Africa will pay much of the human price without having enjoyed the benefits. “Africa only represents 2% of global greenhouse-gas emissions but it is the continent that is expected to suffer the most from climate impacts,” says Mafalda Duarte, who runs the World Bank’s $8bn Climate Investment Funds.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 在肯尼亚中部的山上，茶树在阳光下闪闪发光，几乎呈石灰绿色，农民们对气候变化了如指掌。 “雨季不再可预测，”一位人士说道。 “该下雨的时候却没有下雨，一切都一下子就来了。”气候变化是一个将影响地球上每个人的问题。对于非洲人来说，其后果将特别痛苦：虽然其他地区能够通过燃烧煤炭和石油而致富，但非洲将付出很大的人力代价，却没有享受到好处。世界银行 80 亿美元气候投资基金的负责人马法尔达·杜阿尔特 (Mafalda Duarte) 表示：“非洲仅占全球温室气体排放量的 2%，但预计该大陆将受到气候影响最严重。”

paragraphs.sourceText: B) Although there are huge uncertainties as to the precise impacts of climate change, enough is known to say that global warming represents one of the main threats to Africa’s prosperity. Parts of the continent are already warming much more quickly than the average: temperatures in southern Africa have increased by about twice the global rate over the past 50 years. Even if the world were to cut emissions enough to keep global warming below 1.5 °C, heat-waves would intensify in Africa and diseases would spread to areas not currently affected. Farming would also be hit hard. About 40% of the land now used to grow maize (玉米) would no longer be suitable for it. Overall, it is estimated that maize yields would fall by 18% - 22%.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 尽管气候变化的具体影响存在巨大的不确定性，但众所周知，全球变暖是非洲繁荣的主要威胁之一。非洲大陆部分地区的变暖速度已经远远快于平均水平：过去 50 年来，南部非洲的气温上升速度约为全球的两倍。即使世界减少排放量以将全球变暖控制在 1.5°C 以下，非洲的热浪也会加剧，疾病也会蔓延到目前未受影响的地区。农业也将受到严重打击。现在用于种植玉米的土地中约有 40% 将不再适合种植。总体而言，预计玉米单产将下降 18% - 22%。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Africa is particularly vulnerable, in part because it is already struggling to feed itself and it will have to vastly increase yields and productivity if it is to put food on the plates of a fast-growing population, even without climate change. The UN’s Food and Agriculture Organisation reckons that by 2050 global food production would have to rise by about 70% over its level of 2009 to meet demand from a population that is growing in numbers and appetite. Much of this new demand will be in Africa. Yet the continent already imports about $50bn-worth of food a year and that figure is expected to more than double over the next five years. Self-sufficiency is not Africa’s goal, but the fact that it spends more money importing food than it does buying capital goods suggests it has room for improvement.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 非洲尤其脆弱，部分原因是它已经在养活自己方面陷入困境，即使没有气候变化，如果它想把食物送到快速增长的人口的盘子里，就必须大幅提高产量和生产力。联合国粮食及农业组织估计，到 2050 年，全球粮食产量必须比 2009 年的水平增长约 70%，才能满足人口数量和胃口不断增长的需求。这些新需求大部分来自非洲。然而，非洲大陆每年进口的食品价值约 500 亿美元，预计未来五年这一数字将增加一倍以上。自给自足不是非洲的目标，但非洲在进口粮食上花费的钱多于购买资本货物的事实表明它还有改进的空间。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) Finding out why is not hard. Most farms are tiny, ploughed by hand and reliant on rain. More than half of Africa’s people make their living from farming. Although its total harvest has climbed over the past few decades, this is mainly because there are more people farming more land. But in many places there is no spare land to farm. Plots in Rwanda are so small that you could fit 250 of them onto the average American farm. And although output per worker has improved by more than half over the past 30 years in Africa, that is still far behind the 2.5 times improvement in Asia. Yields of maize are generally less than two tonnes per hectare, a fifth the level in America.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 找出原因并不难。大多数农场都很小，靠手工犁耕，依赖雨水。一半以上的非洲人口以务农为生。尽管过去几十年来其总收成有所上升，但这主要是因为有更多的人耕种更多的土地。但许多地方没有多余的土地可以耕种。卢旺达的土地非常小，一般美国农场可以容纳 250 块土地。尽管非洲工人的人均产出在过去 30 年里提高了一半以上，但仍远远落后于亚洲 2.5 倍的提高。玉米产量通常每公顷不到两吨，是美国水平的五分之一。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) The low productivity of African farmers is reflected in national economic statistics — despite absorbing so much labour, farming generates just 15% of GDP. “They can’t even feed their families,” says Jennifer Blanke, a vice-president of the African Development Bank in charge of agriculture. “Farm productivity hasn’t improved in many parts of Africa for 100 years.”
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 非洲农民的低生产力反映在国家经济统计中——尽管农业吸收了如此多的劳动力，但只产生了 GDP 的 15%。 “他们甚至无法养家糊口，”非洲开发银行负责农业的副行长詹妮弗·布兰克说。 “100 年来，非洲许多地区的农业生产力都没有提高。”

paragraphs.sourceText: F) One reason is that in the first few decades of independence, many African governments neglected farming as they focused on industrialising their economies. Others damaged it by pushing down the prices that state monopolies paid for their crops in order to subsidise workers in cities with cheap food. Ghana taxed cocoa (可可粉) exports so heavily that production collapsed by half between the 1960s and 1980s, despite a jump in the global price of cocoa. Yet over the past two decades or so governments and donors have begun to look again at farming as a way of providing jobs for the 13 million young people entering the workforce each year. Much of the focus has been on getting small farmers to use fertiliser and, more important, better seeds. The results can be impressive. Improved varieties of sorghum (高粱), for instance, can produce a crop that is 40% larger than the usual variety. Infrastructure is important. A World Bank irrigation project in Ethiopia helped farmers increase their potato harvest from about 8 tonnes per hectare to 35 tonnes.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 原因之一是，在独立的最初几十年里，许多非洲政府忽视了农业，而专注于经济工业化。其他人则通过压低国家垄断企业购买农作物的价格来损害它，以便用廉价食品补贴城市工人。加纳对可可粉出口征税过高，导致 20 世纪 60 年代至 80 年代可可粉产量锐减一半，尽管全球可可价格大幅上涨。然而，在过去二十年左右的时间里，各国政府和捐助者开始重新审视农业，将其视为为每年进入劳动力市场的 1300 万年轻人提供就业机会的一种方式。重点是让小农使用化肥，更重要的是，使用更好的种子。结果可能令人印象深刻。例如，改良的高粱品种可以比普通品种的产量增加 40%。基础设施很重要。世界银行在埃塞俄比亚的灌溉项目帮助农民将马铃薯产量从每公顷约 8 吨增加到 35 吨。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) Better techniques help, too. Small coffee farmers in Kenya are able to increase their incomes by 40% by following a few simple guidelines on caring for their bushes, such as trimming all but three of their stems. Many of their neighbours do not follow the advice, because it seems counter-intuitive. More stems ought to lead to more coffee beans, they say. Yet after seeing those following the advice get bigger harvests for a season or two, many others start doing the same.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 更好的技术也有帮助。肯尼亚的小咖啡农通过遵循一些简单的照料灌木丛指南（例如修剪除三根茎以外的所有茎），可以将收入增加 40%。他们的许多邻居不听从这个建议，因为这似乎违反直觉。他们说，更多的茎应该会产生更多的咖啡豆。然而，在看到那些遵循建议的人在一两个季节获得更大的收成后，许多其他人也开始这样做。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) One way of spreading knowledge is to link farms to big buyers of their harvests. When Diageo, a British drinks giant, built a brewery in western Kenya, it wanted to use local crops to make a beer cheap enough to compete with illicit home brew. It organised farmers into groups, improved supply chains for them to get seeds and fertiliser and then agreed to buy their grain. It now provides a market to about 17,000 farmers. Across the region it has doubled its use of local raw material to about 80% over five years, says John O’Keeffe, who runs its Africa business.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 传播知识的一种方法是将农场与其农作物的大买家联系起来。当英国饮料巨头帝亚吉欧 (Diageo) 在肯尼亚西部建造一家啤酒厂时，它希望利用当地农作物生产出足够便宜的啤酒，以与非法自制啤酒竞争。它把农民组织起来，改善供应链，让他们获得种子和化肥，然后同意购买他们的粮食。现在它为大约 17,000 名农民提供了一个市场。负责其非洲业务的约翰·奥基夫 (John O’Keeffe) 表示，五年来，该公司在整个地区对当地原材料的使用量增加了一倍，达到约 80%。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) An even more important change is the move from traditional farming to building businesses that can profitably bring technology and investment to small farms. Taita Ngetich, a young Kenyan, was studying engineering when he wanted to earn a little money on the side. He scraped together 20,000 Kenyan shillings (about $200) to plant tomatoes. Everything went wrong. The crop was attacked by pests. “Then there was a massive flood that swallowed all our capital,” he says. Mr Ngetich persevered by looking into buying a greenhouse to protect his plants from bugs and rain. The cheapest ones cost more than $2,500 each, so he designed his own for half the price. Soon neighbouring farmers started placing orders with him, and now his firm, Illuminum Greenhouses, has sold more than 1,400 greenhouses that provide livelihoods to about 6,000 people. The business does not stop there; he also supplies fertiliser, high-quality seedlings and smart sensors that increase yields.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 一个更重要的变化是从传统农业转向建立可以为小型农场带来技术和投资并有利可图的企业。年轻的肯尼亚人泰塔·恩盖提奇 (Taita Ngetich) 正在学习工程学，当时他想兼职赚点钱。他凑了 20,000 肯尼亚先令（约合 200 美元）来种植西红柿。一切都出了问题。农作物受到害虫的侵袭。 “然后发生了一场大洪水，吞噬了我们所有的资本，”他说。恩盖蒂奇先生坚持不懈地考虑购买温室，以保护他的植物免受虫子和雨水的侵害。最便宜的每件售价超过 2,500 美元，因此他以一半的价格设计了自己的产品。很快，附近的农民开始向他下订单，现在他的公司 Illuminum Greenhouses 已售出 1,400 多个温室，为大约 6,000 人提供了生计。业务并不止于此；他还提供肥料、优质苗木和智能传感器，以提高产量。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Illuminum’s success shows how technology can help even small farms become more productive. Because such a large share of Africa’s population earns a living from agriculture, even small improvements in productivity can lift the incomes of millions of people. But over the longer run small-scale farming can go only so far, especially in the face of climate change and population pressure.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) Illuminum 的成功展示了技术如何帮助小型农场提高生产力。由于非洲很大一部分人口以农业为生，因此即使生产率的微小提高也可以提高数百万人的收入。但从长远来看，小规模农业只能走这么远，特别是在面临气候变化和人口压力的情况下。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) “If we really want to lift people out of poverty we have to finance projects that will get them an income of at least $100 a month so that they can pay for health care and education,” says Mr Ngetich. “Projects that give them an extra $2 a month from growing beans or maize aren’t going to get them there.” Getting those big jumps will need better jobs in factories and cities.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) “如果我们真的想让人们摆脱贫困，我们就必须资助能让他们每月至少获得 100 美元收入的项目，以便他们能够支付医疗保健和教育费用，”Ngetich 先生说。 “通过种植豆类或玉米每月额外给他们 2 美元的项目并不能让他们实现这一目标。”要实现这些巨大的飞跃，就需要工厂和城市提供更好的就业机会。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. It is said that agricultural productivity in many African countries has remained low for a century.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 据说，一个世纪以来，许多非洲国家的农业生产力一直很低。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Building connections between farms and major purchasers of their produce can promote African farmers’ use of advanced farming techniques.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 在农场与其产品的主要购买者之间建立联系可以促进非洲农民使用先进的农业技术。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. Parts of Africa are getting warmer much faster than the average, with southern Africa witnessing roughly twice the global warming rate over the last half century.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 非洲部分地区的变暖速度比平均水平快得多，南部非洲的变暖速度大约是过去半个世纪全球变暖速度的两倍。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. Improved farming practices have enabled Kenyan farmers to increase farm produce remarkably.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 改进的耕作方法使肯尼亚农民的农产品产量显着增加。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Africa is especially susceptible to the effects of global warming partly because it has difficulty feeding its increasing population even without climate change.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: One of the great successes of the Republican Party in recent decades is the relentless propagation of a simple formula for economic growth: tax cuts.
paragraphs.translationZh: 共和党近几十年来的伟大成功之一就是不懈地传播一个简单的经济增长公式：减税。

paragraphs.sourceText: The formula doesn’t work, but that has not affected its popularity. And while the cult of tax cuts has attracted many critics, it lacks for obvious rivals.
paragraphs.translationZh: 该公式不起作用，但这并没有影响它的受欢迎程度。尽管减税崇拜招致了许多批评，但它缺乏明显的竞争对手。

paragraphs.sourceText: Democratic politicians have tended to campaign on helping people left behind by economic growth. When Democrats do talk about encouraging economic growth, they often sound like Republicans.
paragraphs.translationZh: 民主党政治家倾向于在竞选活动中帮助那些因经济增长而落在后面的人。当民主党人确实谈论鼓励经济增长时，他们听起来常常像共和党人。

paragraphs.sourceText: This is not just a political problem for Democrats; it is an economic problem for the United States. The nation needs a better story about the drivers of economic growth. The painful lessons of recent decades point to a promising candidate: higher wages.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这不仅是民主党的政治问题，也是民主党的问题。这对美国来说是一个经济问题。这个国家需要更好地讲述经济增长的驱动力。近几十年来的惨痛教训指出了一个有希望的候选人：更高的工资。

paragraphs.sourceText: Raising the wages of American workers ought to be the priority of economic policymakers. We’d all be better off paying less attention to quarterly updates on the growth of the nation’s gross domestic product (GDP) and focusing instead on the growth of workers’ paychecks.
paragraphs.translationZh: 提高美国工人的工资应该是经济政策制定者的首要任务。我们最好少关注国家国内生产总值 (GDP) 增长的季度更新，而关注工人工资的增长。

paragraphs.sourceText: Set aside, for the moment, the familiar argument for higher wages: fairness. The argument here is that higher wages can fuel the engine of economic growth.
paragraphs.translationZh: 暂时搁置人们熟悉的关于提高工资的论点：公平。这里的论点是，更高的工资可以推动经济增长的引擎。

paragraphs.sourceText: Perhaps the most famous illustration of the benefits is the story of Henry Ford’s decision in 1914 to pay $5 a day to workers on his Model T assembly lines. He did it to increase production — he was paying a premium to maintain a reliable workforce. The unexpected benefit was that Ford’s factory workers became Ford customers, too.
paragraphs.translationZh: 也许最著名的例子就是亨利·福特 (Henry Ford) 1914 年决定向 T 型车装配线上的工人每天支付 5 美元的故事。他这样做是为了增加产量——他支付高价来维持可靠的劳动力。意想不到的好处是，福特工厂的工人也成为了福特的客户。

paragraphs.sourceText: The same logic still holds: Consumption drives the American economy, and workers who are paid more can spend more.
paragraphs.translationZh: 同样的逻辑仍然成立：消费推动美国经济，工资高的工人可以花更多的钱。

paragraphs.sourceText: Mainstream economists insist that it is impossible to order up a sustainable increase in wages because compensation levels reflect the unerring judgment of market forces.
paragraphs.translationZh: 主流经济学家坚持认为，不可能要求工资持续增长，因为薪酬水平反映了市场力量的准确判断。

paragraphs.sourceText: The conventional wisdom held that productivity growth was the only route to higher wages. Through that lens, efforts to negotiate higher wages were counterproductive. Minimum-wage laws would raise unemployment because there was only so much money in the wage pool, and if some people got more, others would get none.
paragraphs.translationZh: 传统观点认为，生产率增长是提高工资的唯一途径。从这个角度来看，谈判提高工资的努力适得其反。最低工资法会提高失业率，因为工资池里的钱只有这么多，如果有些人得到更多，其他人就什么也得不到。

paragraphs.sourceText: It was in the context of this worldview that it became popular to argue that tax cuts would drive prosperity. Rich people would invest, productivity would increase, wages would rise.
paragraphs.translationZh: 正是在这种世界观的背景下，减税将推动繁荣的观点开始流行。富人会投资，生产力会提高，工资会上涨。

paragraphs.sourceText: In the real world, things are more complicated. Wages are influenced by a tug of war between employers and workers, and employers have been winning. One clear piece of evidence is the widening gap between productivity growth and wage growth since roughly 1970. Productivity has more than doubled; wages have lagged far behind.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在现实世界中，事情要复杂得多。工资受到雇主和工人之间拉锯战的影响，而雇主一直是赢家。一个明显的证据是，自 1970 年左右以来，生产率增长与工资增长之间的差距不断扩大。生产率增长了一倍以上；工资已经远远落后了。

paragraphs.sourceText: A focus on wage growth would provide an antidote (矫正方法) to the attractive simplicity of the belief in the magical power of tax cuts.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对工资增长的关注将为减税神奇力量这一简单而有吸引力的信念提供一剂解药。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Journal editors decide what gets published and what doesn’t, affecting the careers of other academics and influencing the direction that a field takes. You’d hope, then, that journals would do everything they can to establish a diverse editorial board, reflecting a variety of voices, experiences, and identities.
paragraphs.translationZh: 期刊编辑决定发表哪些内容，不发表哪些内容，从而影响其他学者的职业生涯并影响一个领域的发展方向。那么，你会希望期刊尽一切努力建立一个多元化的编辑委员会，反映不同的声音、经历和身份。

paragraphs.sourceText: Unfortunately a new study in Nature Neuroscience makes for disheartening reading. The team finds that the majority of editors in top psychology and neuroscience journals are male and based in the United States: a situation that may be amplifying existing gender inequalities in the field and influencing the kind of research that gets published.
paragraphs.translationZh: 不幸的是，《自然神经科学》杂志上的一项新研究读起来令人沮丧。研究小组发现，顶级心理学和神经科学期刊的大多数编辑都是男性，而且居住在美国：这种情况可能会加剧该领域现有的性别不平等，并影响发表的研究类型。

paragraphs.sourceText: Men were found to account for 60% of the editors of psychology journals. There were significantly more male than female editors at each level of seniority, and men made up the majority of editors in over three quarters of the journals. Crucially, the proportion of female editors was significantly lower than the overall proportion of women psychology researchers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究发现，心理学期刊的编辑中男性占 60%。各个级别的男性编辑明显多于女性编辑，超过四分之三的期刊中男性编辑占大多数。至关重要的是，女性编辑的比例明显低于女性心理学研究人员的总体比例。

paragraphs.sourceText: The differences were even starker in the neuroscience journals: 70% of editors were male, and men held the majority of editorial positions in 88% of journals. In this case, the proportion of female editors was not significantly lower than the proportion of female researchers working in neuroscience — a finding that reveals enduring gender disparities in the field more broadly.
paragraphs.translationZh: 神经科学期刊中的差异更为明显：70% 的编辑是男性，男性在 88% 的期刊中担任大部分编辑职位。在这种情况下，女性编辑的比例并不明显低于神经科学领域女性研究人员的比例——这一发现更广泛地揭示了该领域持久的性别差异。

paragraphs.sourceText: Based on their results, the team concludes that “the ideas, values and decision-making biases of men are overrepresented in the editorial positions of the most recognized academic journals in psychology and neuroscience.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 根据他们的研究结果，研究小组得出结论：“在心理学和神经科学领域最受认可的学术期刊的编辑职位中，男性的想法、价值观和决策偏见所占比例过高。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Gender inequality in science is often attributed to the fact that senior academics are more likely to be male, because historically science was male-dominated: it’s argued that as time goes on and more women rise to senior roles, the field will become more equal. Yet this study showed that even the junior roles in psychology journals tended to be held disproportionately by men, despite the fact that there are actually more female than male junior psychology faculty.
paragraphs.translationZh: 科学领域的性别不平等通常归因于高级学者更有可能是男性，因为历史上科学是男性主导的：有人认为，随着时间的推移，越来越多的女性晋升到高级职位，该领域将变得更加平等。然而，这项研究表明，即使是心理学期刊中的初级职位，男性也往往比例过高，尽管实际上初级心理学教员中女性的数量多于男性。

paragraphs.sourceText: This implies that a lack of female academics is not the problem. Instead, there are structural reasons that women are disadvantaged in science. Women receive lower salaries and face greater childcare demands, for instance, which can result in fewer publications and grants — the kinds of things that journals look for when deciding who to appoint. Rather than simply blaming the inequality of editorial boards on tradition, we should be actively breaking down these existing barriers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这意味着缺乏女性学者并不是问题所在。相反，女性在科学领域处于不利地位是有结构性原因的。例如，女性的工资较低，面临更大的育儿需求，这可能会导致出版物和赠款减少——而这些正是期刊在决定任命人选时所寻求的东西。我们不应该简单地将编辑委员会的不平等归咎于传统，而应该积极打破这些现有的障碍。

paragraphs.sourceText: A lack of diversity among journal editors also likely contributes to psychology’s WEIRD problem. If journal editors are largely men from the United States, then they will probably place higher value on papers that are relevant to Western, male populations, whether consciously or not.
paragraphs.translationZh: 期刊编辑之间缺乏多样性也可能导致心理学的奇怪问题。如果期刊编辑主要是来自美国的男性，那么无论有意识还是无意识，他们可能会对与西方男性群体相关的论文给予更高的重视。

paragraphs.translationZh: 51. 鉴于其重要职责，我们期望学术期刊的编辑委员会表现出什么？

paragraphs.translationZh: 54. 根据新研究小组的发现，我们可以得出什么结论？

paragraphs.translationZh: 55. 作者建议我们做什么，而不是简单地将编辑委员会的不平等归咎于传统？
